notes: Route: permissive robots.txt (disallows only /wp-admin/, /wp-content/plugins/, /readme.html, /?page=; Python robotparser matches path only, query URLs allowed) -> WordPress REST controller through the rest_route QUERY form: GET https://www.documentonews.gr/?rest_route=/wp/v2/posts&per_page=100&_fields=link,date&after=2026-09-24T00:00:00&before=2026-10-26T23:59:59&page=N -> 200, JSON array, 100 posts/page, walk pages until a short page or HTTP 400 (past last page). KEY: the pretty route /wp-json/wp/v2/posts returns 401 (blocked), the same controller via ?rest_route= returns 200 - so the API is NOT closed, only its pretty path is. Listed date = date-part of the REST 'date' field (Greek local time, e.g. 2026-10-21T...), which is the site's own publish time; verified against page JSON-LD datePublished on 15 re-fetched articles across the window (15/15 exact match, 0 drift). Result: 4044 unique URLs, 31/31 days covered, 2026-09-30=151, 2026-10-10=85, 2026-10-20=175, min 84 on 2026-10-24. Re-fetched samples: HTTP 200, 6000-13600 chars of text, JSON-LD datePublished exactly the listed date; 10/10 random samples had >=6000 chars, none risky. Abandoned routes: (1) /sitemap.xml index -> monthly urlsets /sitemap-pt-post-2026-09.xml and -10.xml DO serve 200 and look complete (3566+3428 loc/lastmod pairs), but <lastmod> is the MODIFIED time, not publish time: it gave only 14-15 URLs on 2026-09-30 where the REST/JSON-LD truth is 151, and it drifts a post to whatever day it was last re-saved. It remains in the script as a fallback only (lastmod converted UTC->Europe/Athens) if REST ever fails. (2) news-sitemap.xml 200 but holds only the last ~3 days, useless for a 31-day window. (3) /2026/10/10/ date archive 404. (4) /feed/ 200 but only the ~10 latest items, no paging back a month. (5) /wp-json/... 401. Total ~9 probe requests plus ~42 REST page requests, full run 23s warm / ~40s cold, well under the 20-minute limit.
